question_text: A Boeing 777 aircraft has the following breakdown of materials usage: Aluminum alloys - $70 \mathrm{wt} \%$ Composites - $11 \mathrm{wt} \%$ Steel - 11 wt \% Titanium alloys - $7 \mathrm{wt} \%$ Other - $1 \mathrm{wt} \%$. Take the average density of an aluminum alloy to be $2.80 \mathrm{Mg} / \mathrm{m}^3$, the average density for a titanium alloy to be $4.40 \mathrm{Mg} / \mathrm{m}^3$, the average density of steel to be $7.80 \mathrm{Mg} / \mathrm{m}^3$, and the average composite density to be $1.50 \mathrm{Mg} / \mathrm{m}^3$. Ignoring the "other," calculate the average density for the overall structural materials in this aircraft. Give your answer as the value of average_density.The unit of the answer is Mg/m^3.
response:
Using the inverse rule of mixtures (mass fractions given, so density is the harmonic weighted average), and renormalizing the four structural materials to 100% (excluding the 1% "other"):

$$\rho_{\text{avg}} = \frac{1}{\sum w_i/\rho_i}$$

with $w_{\text{Al}}=0.7071,\; w_{\text{Comp}}=0.1111,\; w_{\text{Steel}}=0.1111,\; w_{\text{Ti}}=0.0707$ gives $\rho_{\text{avg}} \approx 2.80\ \mathrm{Mg/m^3}$.

$$\boxed{2.80}$$
